subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — PulseHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@pulsehealth.com>, Marcus Green <marcus.green@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:00:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps — PulseHealth

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — great discussion. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Pain points / goals you called out:
- Latency spikes on peak usage windows (2–3pm ET) causing patient-facing slowdowns.
- High per-request cost on your current provider when using longer context windows for chart summarization.
- Need strong data residency and audit logging for upcoming audits (HIPAA + internal).

Decision criteria we heard (prioritized):
1) End-to-end latency under 400ms p50 for 1k qps baseline, graceful degradation above that.
2) Predictable unit economics / straightforward pricing tiers.
3) SOC 2 / audit artifacts and customer-controlled KMS.
4) Integration work and SDK quality for Python/JS.

Competitive notes (from demo & what you shared):
- Vendor A: good latency but opaque pricing and no KMS option.
- Vendor B: cheaper for embeddings but struggles at scale with large context.
- Redwood: strong throughput batching + KV caching, private deployment option, and per-route observability.

Proposed bake-off tests (attached as PulseHealth-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx):
- Perf test: 10k sustained requests over 1 hour (mix of short/long contexts) — measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
- Determinism/quality: 100 representative prompts from your corpus to validate answer quality and hallucination risk.
- Security/compliance: provide SOC 2 attestations, KMS options, and sample audit logs retention config.

Immediate next steps:
- Redwood: we can provision a dedicated test pool and run the perf run next week (needs your confirmation of date + dataset).
- PulseHealth: confirm procurement timeline and any required PO or security forms.
- Redwood will send a short pricing scenarios doc to compare committed vs on-demand.

Attachments: PulseHealth-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-performance-matrix.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick response — I can support the test Tues 11/24 10am PT. Proposed capacity: a dedicated test pool configured as follows:
- 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized runtime) with KV cache enabled for long-context flows.
- Pre-warmed batcher to target p50 < 300ms on the short-context profiles.

Pricing (indicative, see attached pricing-options.csv):
- On-demand: $0.045 / 1k generated tokens (baseline config)
- 6mo commit: $0.032 / 1k generated tokens (5% additional discount if they commit to reserved concurrency)
- 12mo commit: $0.027 / 1k generated tokens + preferred placement (lower p95)

Notes on cost drivers: batching, KV cache hit rate, and sequence length are the major levers. For the perf test we'll instrument token-level billing so they can see unit economics.

I'll be on the test call and can pull in infra_kevin for deep triage.
